# Generic register example

This is an illustrative tool, not an additional standard or required file
format. [ODD §11.5D](../ODD.md#115d-evidence-and-bounded-decisions) owns the
tracking and reconciliation requirement. FOUNDATIONS P4b owns conservation
of needed step-produced facts; ACTIVATION and EVALUATION own acquisition,
evidence and decisions. An LLM or another tool may provide equivalent
functionality without using this register.

A register helps an actor keep track of the work and reconcile its account
with the authoritative workspace. It holds decisions and other facts a
later actor cannot recover, and points to sources and evidence that can be
re-acquired. It does not replace those sources, supply a new authority or
require every observation to be copied into it.

For example, a team is changing the accepted request sizes of an importer:

| Obligation or matter | Tracked account | Basis and evidence references | Reconciliation needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Support the size limit in the adopted requirement | Implementation prepared; acceptance outstanding | Exact requirement revision, implementation subject and test result | Confirm the tested implementation still matches the current candidate and the requirement is still in force |
| An owner chose an error response for excessive input | Record the decision, its scope and authority reference | The owner's retained decision and the affected requirement | Re-enter if that decision is superseded; the register cannot choose a replacement |
| One environment was not exercised | Residual remains open | Test scope and the unperformed case | Keep the gap visible until evidence or an authorised disposition resolves it |

The column names and storage are incidental. A useful mechanism can answer
what is being pursued, what was decided and by whom, what evidence supports
the current claim, what remains unresolved, and what source change would
require reconciliation. When a material input changes, the affected account
is checked again; historical success is not carried forward as current
success merely because it was recorded.

An LLM-provided mechanism can serve the same purpose if the facts needed at
resumption or handoff remain available to the relevant actor and its claims
can be checked against the declared sources. Unavailable private state does
not meet that requirement. The method requires the functions, not a separate
register artifact or a universal event history.

### New Project

This is the **fixed 3.1.0-rc.3 release bootstrap** for a new Product that
explicitly selects this release. It installs the exact native method and
acquires the separate Product distribution. Existing Products use their actual
basis and an explicit migration plan.

The normal public release titled STDO 3.1.0 selects immutable cut 3.1.0-rc.3.
Its six separately owned Products use that suffix; the Python manager uses
PEP 440 spelling 3.1.0rc3. The following manager recipe selects Git, macOS arm64
and CPython 3.13. It creates a new explicit environment, store and Product
directory. Other platforms use the exact constraints with their own compatible
wheel acquisition and verification; the listed archive does not qualify them.

```sh

STDO_DOWNLOAD_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"

  curl --fail --location --output "$STDO_DOWNLOAD_DIR/$asset" "$STDO_ASSETS/$asset"
done

from pathlib import Path
import hashlib, json, sys
root = Path(sys.argv[1])
release = json.loads((root / 'release.json').read_bytes())
if release.get('tag_name') != 'specification_methodology/v3.1.0-rc.3' or release.get('draft') is not False or release.get('prerelease') is not False:
```

# Read and use STDO 3.1

The [installed reading page](index.html) routes the native **3.1.0-rc.3**
method. Start with [the method index](../README.md) or
[Getting Started](../../plugins/spec/references/GETTING_STARTED.md).
The exact installed standards own meaning; this guide adds no rule, adoption
or work authority.

## Work and context

Resolve the Product's exact installed basis and existing grant. Follow the
[SDLC default](../SDLC_DEFAULTS.md) when the Product has selected it, and use
the native work/review skills with their relative references intact.
The [frame-basis template](../templates/PROJECT_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASIS_TEMPLATE.md#sdlc-default-selection)
offers that selection for authorized adoption. Guidance availability and host
installation do not select a default for an existing Product.

Purpose Context owns context construction and purpose indexes. STDO Skills
owns the receipt-based host bindings. Obtain their matching separately
inventoried directories from
[the Product archive](https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology/releases/download/specification_methodology%2Fv3.1.0-rc.3/stdo-products-v3.1.0-rc.3.zip),
verified through [the release](https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology/releases/tag/specification_methodology%2Fv3.1.0-rc.3)
and its [cohort record](https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology/releases/download/specification_methodology%2Fv3.1.0-rc.3/cohort-release-v3.1.0-rc.3.json).
Follow `stdo_skills/scripts/INSTALLATION.md` and `stdo_skills/GETTING_STARTED.md`
inside that archive. An installed native method assumes no sibling checkout.

Choose the context purpose and index matching the actual native source and
query. `sdlc-workflow/1` and `python-pure-refactor/2` serve different decisions;
the Product catalog and exact applicability determine the selection. Retain
unknown facts, uncovered obligations, source re-entry and assessment limits.
Context coverage does not establish task success or release acceptance.

## Optional visual documentation

Representation Tools, STDO Representation and Axiom Indexer remain separate
Products in the same explicit release cohort. Use their own guides and exact
public manifests. The Skills installer's optional visual binding supplies the
`stdo-project` route. Visual documents explain their selected source and
coverage; they do not replace governing clauses or prove prose semantics.
Context use requires no visual representation or Lean installation.

## Historical material

The [3.0.5-rc.1 release](https://github.com/foolishimp/specification_methodology/releases/tag/specification_methodology%2Fv3.0.5-rc.1)
retains its combined tooling, generated explorers, ABI example, Lean sources,
proof reader, results and original receipts. Acquire that exact historical cut
for those subjects. These runtime and proof payloads are intentionally absent
from the current native package; they are not current-source evidence.
The [release note](../../release/release-note.md) records the successor boundary.

# Assessment: STDO 3.1.0-rc.3 native candidate and its predecessor dispositions

**Verdict: `falsified`.** The native source changes match the owner's rulings and leave no stale consumer references. The disposition record falls short in four places (F1–F4), two of which (F2 and F3) are guards dropped from the source without any record. Nothing outside those findings changes this result.

## Subject and basis

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Native candidate | `specification_methodology/v3/build_tenants/common`, 95 members selected by `method/NATIVE_READY_INVENTORY.json` (inventory SHA-256 `e6d80a24…5e34`, from `freeze.stdout` and `PACKAGE_CHECK.json`) |
| Approved source candidate | `c11c7617…9c57` |
| Disposition record | `.ai-workspace/work/STDO_3_1_RC3_2026-11-18/PREDECESSOR_DISPOSITIONS.json`. It sits in the workspace and is not one of the 95 members. |
| Predecessor | RC2 native `21a9d4b9…`, read as `method/PREDECESSOR_ODD.md` |
| Construction basis | installed `stdo://releases/v3.0.4/` |
| Review law | RELEASE §9, EVALUATION §3–§5, ACTIVATION §5 and §7 |
| Severity scale | 1 highest to 5 lowest. The intake names no scale, so I used the one the earlier reviews in this run used. |

**Claims assessed:**
